recommendation.summary: S5 FD-passing process handoff with identity state transfer (new binary).
justification: goroutine-structure, long-running or start-up code changed: in-process patching would leave old code running in goroutines that never return; a new process starts the new goroutine structure, and the old one is drained and exits
S6 blockers (1): github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/microservices-demo/src/frontend.init: init() runs once at start-up (never re-executed / never returns)
alternatives: Kubernetes rolling update (loses in-memory state, needs surge capacity)
risks: new package-level variable github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/microservices-demo/src/frontend.packagingServiceUrl: under S6 it lives in the patch plugin and is re-initialised by every later patch generation
no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 3 functions
3 patched functions are in package main; a Go plugin cannot import package main, so hotpatchgen must relocate them into an importable package
type information is partial (408/408 type errors old/new; third-party packages are opaque): call-graph and state reachability are lower bounds
quiescence: old activations of main(), init-started or long-running goroutines never return, so the old process is retired by exit, not by draining; set a drain deadline in the S5 upgrader
